<teammate-message teammate_id="feed-empty-diagnosis" color="red" summary="FIXED #2944: app-owned projection_rev frozen at 0 froze rev-aware host caches. PR #2952">
FIXED end-to-end. PR #2952: https://github.com/pablof7z/nostr-multi-platform/pull/2952 (Closes #2944).

## Root cause (this IS the device bug, and it's NMP)
Running the real tui shell confirmed the pure-Rust stack renders (real C-ABI `nmp_app_open_feed` + `compose_chirp_runtime` + `Difference(follows,mute)` + `decode_op_feed_snapshot` all surface the notes). So the break is host-side — and I found it: BOTH the generated iOS `ProjectionCache.generated.swift:177` and the Android `ProjectionCache.kt:194` (the NMP-owned rev-aware host apply caches) skip a `Changed` row when `incomingRev <= cached.rev`. App-owned keys like `chirp.timeline.home` emit `projection_rev = 0` on EVERY tick (they're absent from the kernel's builtin rev manifest — `rung2_stamp.rs:31-33`). So the host commits the FIRST (empty) home-feed frame at rev 0, then skips every later card-bearing frame (`0 <= 0`) → frozen empty while the envelope rev (your "decodedRev") climbs to 26. That is exactly "decodedRev advanced to 26 yet no card."

I was wrong in layers 4/5 to call projection_rev=0 "inert" — it's inert for the Rust state-based merge cache, but FATAL for the rev-aware host caches. The kernel was violating its own `projection_rev` wire contract (ADR-0070 Rung 2: rev advances on content change) for app-owned keys.

## The fix (single wire-contract fix → all platforms)
`ProjectionRevTracker::stamp_app_owned_revs`: for app-owned (non-manifest) keys, derive a content-driven rev — a per-key counter that increments when the payload fingerprint changes — so the rev advances iff content changed. Cleared rows keep 0; Tier-2 built-ins untouched. Now `chirp.timeline.home` emits rev 1 (empty) → rev 2 (cards), so the host guard `2 <= 1` is false → it decodes the card frame → renders. Fixes iOS + Android + web at once (no per-platform host patch needed).

Done — standing down.

1. Doc nits → NMP PR #2957 (https://github.com/pablof7z/nostr-multi-platform/pull/2957), branch docs/2944-projection-rev-nits off merged master. All three applied:
   - rung3_omit.rs: reworded the "single pure function, no side-effects" line (stamp_typed_projections now threads `&mut ProjectionRevTracker`); clarified the omit pass itself stays pure.
   - projection_rev/mod.rs header: scoped "NOT content-hash-as-gate" to Tier-2 built-ins and noted app-owned keys are content-driven by necessity (opaque payloads, no dep table).
   - app_owned_revs: documented that Cleared entries are never pruned (monotonicity over memory) so a re-opened key resumes above its last-emitted rev.
   Verified: cargo check -p nmp-core clean, full doctrine_lint_smoke 210 green. Doc-only, should sail through.

2. Chirp PR #44: dropped the real-shell C-ABI guard per your call (the NMP emitted-frame test is authoritative; the recompute one was a weaker duplicate). PR #44 now contains ONLY the two Android host live-path tests (homeFeedLivePathFreezesOnStuckProjectionRev / RendersOnAdvancingProjectionRev, both green on :app:testDebugUnitTest). Heads-up: while trimming, a `git add -A` had accidentally swept in some unrelated apps/tui working-tree edits (a revert of chirp#21 toast handling) — I caught it and restored those files to origin/master, so #44 is now a clean single-file diff (OpFeedDecoderTest.kt only). If you'd rather keep Chirp lean and rely solely on the NMP guard, close #44 — no objection; I kept it because the host live-path coverage is the exact layer that let #2944 slip past golden fixtures. Your call.
